contextual.summary: Loughborough makes Access Loughborough contextual offers up to two grades lower than the typical offer to applicants who had free school meals, or who attend a state school or college and live in an IMD quintile 1 area; Realising Opportunities and LUDUS Gold students get reduced alternative offers (up to two and up to three grades lower).
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to two grades lower than typical entry requirements (Access Loughborough); up to three grades lower with LUDUS Gold

criteria.detail: Known to be eligible for free school meals at the end of Key Stage 4 (Year 11) and/or the six years before it (England; equivalent rules for Northern Ireland and Wales), or currently receiving free school meals or free meals in further education
Live in an area in IMD quintile 1 (England only) AND attend a non-fee-paying (state) school or college
Taking part in Realising Opportunities: you get a dual offer including an alternative offer up to two grades lower, dependent on completing the programme
Taking part in LUDUS Gold: you get a dual offer including an alternative offer up to three grades lower, dependent on completing the programme
Spent more than three months in care (considered as contextual information; not listed as an Access Loughborough criterion)
Have caring responsibilities (young carer); supporting evidence from your referee is needed
Recognised refugee, asylum seeker or granted humanitarian protection
Disability or long-term health condition (supporting evidence from your referee needed)
Mature applicant: aged 21 or over at the start of the course
Other personal or extenuating circumstances that disrupted your education

contextual.rulesText: You're eligible for an Access Loughborough Contextual Offer if you were known to be eligible for free school meals (or currently receive them), or you attend a state school or college and live in IMD quintile 1 (England only). It is open to applicants taking three A levels, or two A levels plus an accepted Level 3 qualification, who expect to pay UK fees. If you're eligible, any offer will be up to two grades lower than typical, but eligibility doesn't guarantee an offer. Other contextual information (care, caring responsibilities, disability, estrangement, refugee status, mature age, extenuating circumstances) is considered individually and may lead to a reduced offer of up to one grade lower.

source.evidence: Where specific contextual information is met, you will be eligible for an Access Loughborough Contextual Offer. This is up to two grades lower than typical entry requirements.

programmes.name: LUDUS Gold
programmes.summary: A free programme of online and on-campus support (including a Business and Economics taster day, an online academic skills project and a VIP open day) for targeted Year 12 students; completing it earns a reduced alternative offer.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students at a state school or college who are UK fee paying, predicted or achieved 5 GCSEs at grades 9-5 (with at least grade 4 in Maths and English Language), and who meet at least one of: live in an IMD quintile 1 area (England), free school meals in the last six years, or time spent in care.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Must meet at least one of: living in an area more deprived than at least 80% of neighbourhoods in England (IMD quintile 1) based on your home postcode; eligible for free school meals in the last 6 years; time spent in care. AND all of: predicted/achieved 5 GCSEs grades 9-5; at least grade 4 in GCSE Maths and English Language; attending a state school/college in Year 12 (or first year of college); UK fee paying (or expecting to be).
benefits: Reduced alternative offer at Loughborough: up to 3 A-level grades lower than the standard offer, if you complete the programme
Priority booking for an Inspiring Minds academic taster day (Business and Economics is one of the events)
VIP Open Day experience for students who complete the programme
Opportunity Scholarship of £3,000 a year for three years (excluding a placement year) if you get an offer, make Loughborough your firm choice and have a verified household income of £30,000 or less
programmes.offerReduction: Up to 3 A level grades lower than the standard offer
programmes.subjects: All subjects (Business and Economics taster day available)

notes: All course facts are for September 2027 entry; Loughborough hasn't published 2028-entry pages yet.

Economics, Economics and Finance and Economics and Management say A-level Maths is not essential, but they need GCSE Maths grade 6 (grade 5 for Finance and Accounting and Finance). Mathematics with Economics needs A-level Maths at grade A.
Every course has a 4-year version with an optional placement year (separate UCAS code) and a year abroad option; the placement year fee is 20% of the full-time fee and a study-abroad year 15%.
Loughborough doesn't normally include the EPQ in offer conditions; it may be used when considering an application after exam results.
Realising Opportunities gives a dual offer up to two grades lower than typical; LUDUS Gold gives one up to three A-level grades lower. Both are recorded as alternative offers on each course.
Many courses get a large number of applications per place, and meeting the typical offer doesn't guarantee an offer.
Business and Management BSc (N202, typical offer AAB) was not added, to keep to 8 courses.
